original_question: Can we see on the induced action φ if Φ is smoothable or not?
target_in_paper: Section 6.1, Question 6.1, together with the paper’s explicit reformulation in Question 6.2. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct two objects—the induced action φ and the smoothability problem for the underlying action Φ—and it is essentially the wording of Question 6.1 in the paper. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
missing_details: Φ is not an arbitrary map: it is a group action Φ: G → Homeo_+(R^2). ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The ambient geometric structure is essential: Φ must preserve two transverse foliations F^+ and F^- of the plane, and the paper allows these foliations to have prong singularities. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

φ is specifically the induced action φ: G → Homeo_+(S^1) on the circle at infinity associated to the pair (F^+, F^-). ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The draft does not make the paper’s intended meaning of “smoothable” stand-alone. Question 6.2 clarifies that the relevant issue is whether the same circle action can be induced by some smooth action Ψ on R^2 preserving two transverse foliations. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The quantifier structure is missing: the reformulated version asks whether there exists an action φ on S^1 induced by a topological action Φ, but not induced by any smooth action Ψ with the same type of foliation-preserving property. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
refined_question: Let Φ: G → Homeo_+(R^2) be a topological group action on the plane preserving two transverse foliations F^+ and F^- (possibly with prong singularities), and let φ: G → Homeo_+(S^1) be the induced action on the circle at infinity associated to the pair (F^+, F^-). Can one determine from φ alone whether Φ is smoothable, in the sense that the same induced circle action arises from some smooth action on R^2 preserving two transverse foliations? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Is there an action φ on S^1 that is induced by a topological action Φ on R^2 preserving two transverse foliations, but is not induced by any smooth action Ψ on R^2 preserving two transverse foliations? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 6.1 rather than any earlier conjecture: it matches Question 6.1 almost verbatim. The only paper-critical context omitted from the draft is the full setup defining Φ and φ, namely an orientation-preserving action on R^2 preserving a transverse pair of foliations and its induced action on the associated circle at infinity. Since the paper itself immediately says “We can reformulate the question as follows” and then states Question 6.2, that reformulation is the unique alternate formulation justified by the text, and it is exactly what makes the notion of smoothability precise without broadening the problem. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
